SMTO-HTTP-0055 — This way of changing a saved sign-in is no longer available

GUID: 30231ec6-291d-4a33-9234-e0a27c87572f
Slug: http-literal-credentials-required
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • Something tried to update a connection's password or key using an older method that SMTO has removed. Nothing was changed; your saved connection is the same as before.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If an SMTO page has been open since before SMTO was updated, reload it in your browser. An older copy of the page may still be using the removed method.
  2. Open Parameter Store, select the connection, choose Reveal & edit value, and enter the new password, key or token in the Authentication section. The connection editor is the supported place to change sign-in details and keeps them in protected fields.
  3. Select Save, then select Test connection. The test shows straight away whether the service accepts the new sign-in details.

What success looks like

  • Test connection reports the connection as Reachable and Authenticated.

If it still fails

  • If a script or another tool sent this request, it needs to be changed to save the whole connection instead. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The retired per-connection credentials route (POST /api/agent/http/connections/…/credentials) always returns HTTP 410; it does not read or store the submitted values, so the saved connection is unchanged.

What this means

  • The obsolete replace-credentials endpoint unconditionally returns HTTP 410 instead of editing the saved connection. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The obsolete replace-credentials endpoint unconditionally returns HTTP 410 instead of editing the saved connection.

How to diagnose it

  • Check which UI/client called the removed endpoint and use the current supported editor.

How to fix it

  • Update credentials by saving the full literal HTTP connection profile, including its auth fields, through the Parameter Store editor or the connection's PUT route under /api/agent/http/connections/. Update any script, bookmark or stale browser tab that still calls the retired …/credentials route.
  • Edit authentication values in the supported connection profile editor, keeping secrets in their designated private fields.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended values are updated through the current connection flow.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
